finding.title: Modal validation prevents result-only recovery for an existing operation when the live draft has 0 or 21 food photos
finding.phase: ReviewModal submit admission before ReviewSaveOperation readback
counterexample: A valid operation uploads and dispatches insert; the insert commits but its reply and first readback are uncertain, so the modal reports blocked and retains the operation.
The live draft later contains zero food photos, which is directly reachable by removing all photos after the blocked result, or contains 21 photos from a restored legacy over-limit draft.
The normal submit controls are disabled because canSubmitReview is false.
Even a direct handleSubmit invocation returns at the maximum or required-field validation before saveOperation.submit.
ReviewSaveOperation therefore cannot read the original operation and convert the committed row into saved-previous while preserving the changed live draft.
finding.impact: The UI instructs the operator to retry in the same composer, but the only operation-aware retry path is unreachable for these invalid current drafts. Closing may run cancellation readback, but it closes and clears the current draft instead of providing the saved-previous edit recovery contract.
finding.test_gap: Operation-level tests prove 21-photo saved-previous and unknown readback directly, while ReviewModal-level tests cover only a new 21-photo submission. No modal test covers a retained unknown operation followed by a 0-photo or 21-photo live draft.

confirmed_fixed_boundaries: Exactly 20 food photos retain the complete prepare, upload, and insert path.
A new 21-photo operation fails before operation id allocation, prepare, upload, insert, or cleanup.
Photo-only and OCR-bound app submissions share ReviewSaveOperation's maximum.
The OCR save route imports the same maximum and rejects counts outside 1 through 20.
The prior 48-photo uncertainty fixture now binds its maximum parallel boundary to 20.
required_resolution_contract: Expose a result-only recovery path for an existing operation that is callable even when the current live draft fails new-submission validation.
Recovery must inspect only the retained operation and must not allocate a new id, capture a replacement draft, prepare files, upload, insert, or delete current draft input.
A verified committed original operation must surface saved-previous and preserve the current 0-photo or 21-photo live draft for editing.
An unavailable, mismatched, or absent readback must remain blocked under the existing uncertainty rules.
The UI must expose the recovery action while normal submission remains disabled for an invalid live draft.
Add modal-level counterexamples for both 0 and 21 photos with prepare, upload, insert, and new-id counts fixed at zero during recovery.
evidence_limits: This event records source-order analysis only; owner test results were not repeated.
No hosted database, Storage, provider, browser, application server, deployment, commit, push, or sealed evidence mutation was performed.
